summary.headline: Mastek Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.4% QoQ cc to $107.3M, but 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M and EBITDA margin slipped to 14.4%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 2.4% QoQ in constant currency to $107.3M (Rs 1,018.7 crore, up 8.3% YoY in INR), with PAT of Rs 105.7 crore. Operating EBITDA margin fell about 100 bps QoQ to 14.4%, mainly from increments and ESOPs (190 bps), partly offset by AI-led efficiency and extra working days. The 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M, attributed to a delayed US federal start and slower UK consumption, though it grew 2.3% YoY in USD. Management reiterated that FY27 should beat FY26, with North America turning around from H2 and UK Healthcare recovering after recontracting.

financial_highlights.change: -7.7% QoQ, +2.3% YoY in USD, +10.4% YoY in INR

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and investments (net of debt)
financial_highlights.change: up about Rs 36 crore after Rs 50 crore dividend and Rs 55 crore loan repayment

segments.name: UK-Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4.1% in the quarter, and UK EBIT was 18%. Financial Services grew over 16% QoQ, and public sector grew 6.1% QoQ. Healthcare & Life Sciences lagged on right-shifted starts, and several public-sector orders were put on hold pending the new government's budget.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Total backlog rose 7.8% QoQ and 47.9% YoY. Management expects a meaningful growth turnaround from H2, though a $25M federal deal start has slipped to after the mid-term elections.

segments.name: APAC & Middle East
segments.commentary: Some older contracts were signed, giving a revenue bounce-back in Q2. Management said the Middle East outlook is uncertain and performance is well below plan, especially in Saudi Arabia.

segments.name: Verticals
segments.commentary: Public sector grew 6.1% QoQ and Financial Services grew 15.3% QoQ. Healthcare & Life Sciences has been slow for two quarters, with management expecting recovery after beta-phase contract awards in Q3 or early Q4.

guidance_outlook: Margin target: improve EBITDA by at least 160 bps in the medium term, with the return to the 16% mark dependent on macro and geopolitical factors.
US and Middle East margins expected to improve from Q3, which should offset some of the UK mix-driven margin loss.
FY27 expected to beat FY26, with H2 seen as no slower than H1, though management flagged Middle East and geopolitical risk.
North America expected to see a meaningful growth turnaround from H2.
A UK NHS-related data transformation contract (north of GBP 100M) is an H2 event and would be incremental to TCV; a bridge contract covers about six months.
Subcontracting expected to stay around 18-20% of revenue, moving by about one percentage point in the short term.
Revenue and AI metrics, plus a Data & AI horizontal split, to be disclosed from next quarter (Q3 FY27).
capex_capacity: Headcount closed at 4,810, down 87 QoQ due to workforce restructuring and a change in onsite/offshore mix.
Utilisation including trainees fell 0.8% QoQ, reflecting investment in domain resources.
Sale of Chennai property completed, booked as an exceptional gain, offset by restructuring costs and a write-off of old receivables (one-time).
Attrition (LTM) fell to 15.2% from 16.4%, the second consecutive quarterly decline.
Added 18 new customers in the quarter versus 13 in Q1.
demand_pricing: AI deals made up more than 40% of deals won in the quarter, and about 45% of the total order book. 53 AI deals were closed.
AI transformation deals run at roughly $0.5M to $5M each. AI productivity takeout deals can be much larger, with a $10M+ North America life sciences win.
AI transformation and foundation deals earn 40%+ gross margin, sometimes above 50%. AI productivity deals are price-aggressive with compressed margins.
Project business rose to 44-45% of revenue from about 40%, mostly fixed-bid. UK public sector and healthcare buy on rate cards.
Average deal tenure is about 3 years plus 2 years in UK-Europe and 18-24 months in North America.
Pipeline includes $100M+ deals to be adjudicated over 6-9 months.
Healthcare softness in UK-Europe is tied to the alpha-to-beta recontracting gap and a ramp-down in an offshore UK healthcare account.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book weakness execution-led or UK pressure? Is FY27 still expected to beat FY26? What is the ramp on new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: A $25M US federal deal start was delayed until after the mid-term elections, and a UK contract is consuming more slowly than planned, with pickup expected around Q4. Management still expects FY27 to beat FY26, citing H2 strength in UK and US and a Middle East dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are AI deals from new or existing clients, what are the deal sizes, and when will AI revenue be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: AI deals come from both new and existing clients, with at least two net-new wins in the examples shown. Typical AI deal size is $0.5M-$5M, and AI revenue figures will be presented from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline, and what is the bridge to the 160 bps recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments and ESOPs cost 190 bps. A UK mix shift from high-margin projects to lower-margin sovereignty and security-cleared work cost about 200 bps. AI-led efficiencies and restructuring recovered about 200 bps. Forex was a 20 bps tailwind. US and Middle East margins are expected to improve from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is North America growth muted, and how do BFSI and healthcare trends differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a North America turnaround from H2. Healthcare & Life Sciences remains its strongest vertical, and BFSI growth is mainly UK-led. North America financial services is still early-stage.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI deals grow after the initial POC, and what margins do they earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI engagements typically expand into more process areas after the first win. Transformation and foundation deals earn 40%+ gross margin, while AI productivity deals carry compressed margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter energy and utilities, and what is the Top 5/Top 10 trend and subcon outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The energy and utilities push uses the public-sector framework playbook, with three frameworks landed in 90-120 days. Subcontracting is 18-20% of revenue and may move about one point; UK localisation and security-cleared demand may drive short-term subcon increases.

risks_watch: UK policy and budget uncertainty after the change of PM. Public-sector orders have been put on hold or cancelled pending budgets, and social care is a possible new focus.
Middle East and Saudi Arabia uncertainty, with performance well below plan.
Slower consumption on the US federal deal and UK contracts, which could keep the 12-month backlog soft.
Healthcare & Life Sciences recovery depends on beta-phase contract awards expected in Q3 or early Q4.
UK security-cleared and localisation demand, which pressures margins and T&M economics. Around 60-65% of business is UK, primarily T&M.
Margin recovery pace is tied to macro factors. Management has not committed to a timeline for returning to 16%.
Disclosure is changing: the horizontal split and AI revenue will be reworked from Q3, and the factsheet client metrics were redefined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term AI transformation story and the H2 turnaround, but cautious and somewhat defensive on near-term order book softness, UK public-sector timing, the Middle East, and margin recovery velocity, which it repeatedly tied to external factors.
key_quotes: Our endeavor will be to improve by at least 160 bps in the medium term. However, the velocity of improvement will be to some extent dependent upon macro and geopolitical factors.
A DSO of 74 days is one of the best in the industry, reflecting our current cash management and aggressive collection initiative.
AI transformative kind of deals, I believe initially would be small, but they'll be more evolving into larger deals instead of the customer signing one large deal at a go.
So the 12-month backlog number is an indicator of where we see the business moving as on date when we share that number.

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 will beat FY26 and guided North America to a meaningful turnaround from H2, backed by a $286.2M 12-month backlog (+2.3% YoY USD) and a >GBP100M NHS contract as an H2 event, though the backlog fell 7.7% QoQ and the $25M US federal start slipped, so support is partial.
